target.title: fix(active-memory): keep recall circuit breaker tripped across cooldown
target.body:
Closes #100167 ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where agents with the `active-memory` plugin enabled pay a fixed recall-timeout stall (~15s by default) on **every** turn once recall starts failing, instead of the plugin backing off. The reporter saw `status=timeout summaryChars=0` on every `main`-agent turn for 24+ hours, making latency-sensitive flows (Talk / live voice, direct chat) feel unresponsive. The plugin already has a circuit breaker (#74054) that is supposed to skip recall after `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts` consecutive timeouts. But on cooldown expiry it **deleted the failure record entirely**. At normal turn cadence — turns spaced further apart than `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` (default 60s, max 10m) — the consecutive-timeout count reset to zero before it could ever reach the threshold, so the breaker never re-engaged and every turn ran the sub-agent into the watchdog again. ## Why This Change Was Made Make the breaker **half-open** across the cooldown instead of resetting ([`extensions/active-memory/index.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.ts)): - After the cooldown, allow a single **probe** recall through but keep the tripped record. A probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately (one recorded timeout, not `maxTimeouts` fresh ones); a successful recall clears it via the existing `resetCircuitBreaker` path. - Track the in-flight probe so only one runs at a time, and **self-heal**: if a probe is lost (aborted without recording a timeout or success), another is allowed once a full cooldown has elapsed — the breaker can never stick permanently open and silently disable recall. ## User Impact A persistently failing agent/model now pays the recall timeout **at most once per cooldown window** instead of on every turn. Recovery is unchanged — the next successful recall clears the breaker. Existing config (`circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs`) is unchanged; docs updated to describe the half-open behavior. ## Scope / Honest Limitations This is deliberately scoped to the **recurring per-turn timeout tax**, which is the measurable user impact. It does **not** change *why* the embedded recall run produces zero model output (`payloads=0`, `stopReason=missing`) on the reporter's specific stack (openai `gpt-5.5` + codex app-server + `lossless-claw` per-turn projection). Notably, the issue's suggested root cause (empty prompt from `assembledMessages: 0`) does not hold up in code: [`context-engine-projection.ts`](extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts) falls back to the raw recall prompt as `promptText` when there is no assembled context, and that text is sent to Codex — so the prompt is not empty. Pinning down the real zero-output cause needs a live repro on that provider stack, which is why triage labeled the issue `needs-live-repro`. That part is left for a follow-up with live evidence. One known limitation of this fix: turns spaced further apart than the maximum cooldown (10m) still probe on each turn by design; operators on very low-cadence chats can raise `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` to widen protection. ## Evidence Focused unit tests added in [`extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`](extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts): - After the cooldown, one probe is allowed through, the tripped record is retained (not deleted), and a **single** probe timeout re-opens the breaker immediately — the exact regression behind #100167. - A lost half-open probe lets another probe through after a further cooldown (no permanent stick), and a successful recall clears the breaker. Existing breaker tests (skip-within-cooldown, `circuit breaker open` log, reset-on-success) remain valid under the new behavior. > Note: I could not run the suite locally — this monorepo requires `pnpm@11` and Node `>=22.19` (not available in my environment), so CI runs the tests. --- ## Behavior proof (after fix) Real capture from the openai/`gpt-5.5` + codex app-server + `lossless-claw` stack isn't available to me (that's the `needs-live-repro` gate). But this fix is a state-machine change, so here is deterministic terminal output that exercises the **exact breaker logic from this PR** (old vs new functions, virtual clock) against a recall that always times out — i.e. the condition reported in #100167 where every turn logs `status=timeout summaryChars=0`: ```text active-memory recall breaker — recall always times out (as in #100167) config: maxTimeouts=3 cooldown=60s timeout=15s == Talk / live-voice cadence (30 turns, 3s apart) == OLD: ran=6/30 dead-time=90s RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip NEW: ran=4/30 dead-time=60s RUN RUN RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip skip RUN skip skip skip skip skip skip skip == Direct chat, brisk cadence (20 turns, 20s apart) == OLD: ran=12/20 dead-time=180s RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN RUN RUN skip skip NEW: ran=8/20 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip RUN skip skip == Sparse cadence (turns > cooldown apart) (8 turns, 3600s apart) == OLD: ran=8/8 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN NEW: ran=8/8 dead-time=120s RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN ``` Reading it: - **Brisk direct chat** is the clearest: OLD re-runs **3** recalls every cooldown cycle (`RUN RUN RUN skip skip …`, 180s dead-time), NEW re-runs only **1** (`RUN skip skip …`, 120s) because the tripped record is retained instead of deleted. - **Talk / live-voice** cadence: OLD 6 runs, NEW 4 — and NEW stays skipped far longer after tripping. - **Sparse cadence** (turns further apart than the cooldown): OLD == NEW, both probe every turn. This is the documented limitation — the fix caps repeated timeouts within a cooldown window, it can't help traffic slower than the cooldown. Operators raise `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` for that.
Reproduce (plain node, no deps) The script mirrors `isCircuitBreakerOpen` / `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout` from `extensions/active-memory/index.ts` verbatim and simulates turn sequences. The same logic is covered by the unit tests in `extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`, which CI runs against the real module.
